findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass` while StatefulDetectorHandler declares get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data as @abc.abstractmethod, so the class retains a non-empty __abstractmethods__ set and any instantiation raises TypeError. The detector_handler property in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py instantiates the handler class (detector.detector_handler(detector)) when a detector of this type is processed; the first detector registered with this grouptype slug will crash process_detectors with TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, rather than degrade gracefully as the old stub returning [] did.

[ADVISORY] process_detectors deletes the duplicate-group-key guard that logged 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' and now relies on evaluate() returning a dict, so a handler whose evaluate() implementation produces colliding keys silently overwrites the earlier result with no log. The stated invariant ('This shouldn't happen - log an error and continue on, but we should investigate') is only enforced for StatefulDetectorHandler by dict construction, not for raw DetectorHandler subclasses (e.g. MockDetectorHandler in tests can return dict literals with repeated keys by different paths); a third-party handler returning a dict built with duplicate keys loses detections silently instead of surfacing the error log, and the corresponding regression test (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted rather than adapted.

[BUG] StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now stores results in a dict keyed by group_key, so duplicate group keys in a packet silently overwrite the earlier result instead of being detected, and the previous 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error path was deleted with no replacement. A data packet containing two entries with the same group key produces only one occurrence (last-wins) with no error log or metric, silently dropping the duplicate-detection guarantee the old code and its dedicated test (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe, deleted in this diff) enforced; operators lose the signal that should trigger investigation.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now `pass` on StatefulDetectorHandler, which declares build_occurrence_and_event_data (and evaluate) as @abc.abstractmethod, so instantiating the handler raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Any detector whose type resolves to this grouptype reaches handler = self.detector_handler ... handler.evaluate(data_packet) in process_detectors and crashes with TypeError instead of producing results — the old stub returned [] safely. The diff removes the previous evaluate override without implementing the new abstract method, so the acceptance path for this grouptype is broken the moment it is exercised.

[ADVISORY] Coverage for the OK/resolved path never verifies the Kafka production side: all new produce_occurrence_to_kafka assertions only cover the occurrence (non-OK) branch, and no test exercises process_detectors delivering a StatusChangeMessage end-to-end. A regression that fails to produce or mis-shapes the resolve payload (e.g. swapping status_change and occurrence args in create_issue_occurrence_from_result) passes the suite, because the resolution branch's serialization is only checked at the evaluate() level, not at the producer boundary the way the occurrence branch now is.

[ADVISORY] The new occurrence branch is only tested for HIGH priority; no test drives evaluate_group_key_value to a different non-OK DetectorPriorityLevel, leaving the PriorityLevel(new_status) conversion and occurrence priority propagation unverified for MEDIUM/LOW. If a detector condition maps to a priority whose value does not round-trip through sentry's PriorityLevel (or if initial_issue_priority is set wrongly for lower severities), no test in this diff catches it, and incidents would be filed with the wrong initial priority once real handlers implement build_occurrence_and_event_data.

[BUG] The change casts the state-machine's DetectorPriorityLevel to the user-facing PriorityLevel via a bare constructor conversion `PriorityLevel(new_status)` with no mapping or validation layer between the two enums. If DetectorPriorityLevel values ever diverge from PriorityLevel's value assignments (e.g. PriorityLevel reorders its members or adds a MEDIUM between HIGH and OK), detectors will emit occurrences with a higher/lower user-visible severity than the detector state machine intended, silently mislabeling alert priority; nothing in this diff pins the two enums to matching values.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is switched to inherit StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), making the class uninstantiable. Any code path that constructs a MetricAlertDetectorHandler (e.g. detector.detector_handler for a detector whose type is the metric-alert grouptype) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, turning what was previously a harmless stub returning [] into a hard crash for that detector type.

[ADVISORY] The refactor drops the duplicate-group-key guard (error log + skip) entirely with no replacement invariant, so duplicate keys now silently overwrite via the results dict. A handler that ever produces two evaluations for the same group key in one packet now silently emits only the last result, and the operator-visible error signal ('Duplicate detector state group keys found') that existed to trigger investigation is gone, so the previously-detected contract violation becomes invisible.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler (whose evaluate() calls abstract get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values/build_occurrence_and_event_data) but implements none of them, so instantiating it or routing a packet through it raises TypeError instead of returning the old empty list. Any registry path that resolves this handler and calls evaluate() crashes with TypeError (abstract method not implemented) rather than no-oping as before; the old explicit `return []` stub was removed while the subclass still has no concrete methods.

[BUG] The newly activated occurrence path flows detector.project_id (hardcoded `return 1` per the XXX comment) into IssueOccurrence.project_id, so every produced occurrence is stamped with project 1. Once build_occurrence_and_event_data is implemented for real handlers, occurrences are produced to Kafka with project_id=1 regardless of the detector's actual project, misattributing issues in the issues platform.

[ADVISORY] Switching evaluate() results to a dict keyed by group_key silently overwrites duplicate group keys, deleting the only detection path for the invariant the previous code explicitly logged as an error ('Duplicate detector state group keys found'). A handler bug producing colliding group keys now silently drops one result (and its occurrence) instead of surfacing the error log that the old code said was needed to investigate; the integrity check is gone with no replacement.

[BUG] The removed duplicate-group-key guard is silently replaced by dict last-wins overwrite, eliminating the error signal the previous implementation deliberately emitted. When a data packet produces two results for the same group key, the old code logged 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' at error level and skipped the duplicate; the new code (`results[result.group_key] = result`) silently overwrites the earlier result with no log, so the condition the old comment said 'we should investigate' becomes invisible in production and one status change is dropped without any trace. The dedicated test (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted rather than adapted, so the behavior change was never explicitly accepted.

[ADVISORY] test_state_results_multi_group builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with value=6 while the packet supplies 10, and the assertion still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its `value` argument entirely. The in-hook contract promises the occurrence is produced from the evaluated value; the test fixture hardcodes the same value (6) for every group and never asserts on it, so a regression where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives or embeds the wrong value (e.g. swapped keys, stale value from another group) ships green. Staff-level concern: the new coverage added in this diff cannot detect value-handling regressions in the exact behavior it was written to cover.

[ADVISORY] Adding build_occurrence_and_event_data as an @abc.abstractmethod on StatefulDetectorHandler is a breaking public-surface change to every existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclass outside this diff. Any out-of-tree or not-yet-migrated StatefulDetectorHandler subclass that only implemented get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values now fails at instantiation with TypeError (abstract method not implemented), turning what reads as a 'add a hook' change into a forced migration; the diff updates only the test mock and does not enumerate or verify the full set of concrete subclasses.

[BUG] Every occurrence/event_data assertion in this diff is a tautology: the expected values are built by build_mock_occurrence_and_event, the exact same function the MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data implementation (line 35-38) delegates to, so the tests compare the code under test against itself and can never detect wrong occurrence content. If build_occurrence_and_event_data or the routing in evaluate_group_key_value passes wrong arguments (wrong group_key, wrong status, wrong fingerprint), the tests still pass as long as both sides call the same helper with the same arguments; proof: in test_state_results_multi_group the expected occurrence_2 is built with value=6 while the packet's group_2 value is 10, and the test passes because the helper ignores `value` entirely — a regression that propagated the wrong observed value into occurrences would be invisible.

[ADVISORY] The `value` parameter of build_mock_occurrence_and_event is dead — it is never referenced in the function body — yet every call site passes a value, creating the false impression that occurrence content depends on the observed value. The next implementer wiring real occurrence construction will copy this signature and tests will continue passing with any value, so a real handler bug that emits the wrong metric value in occurrences/evidence_data gets no coverage; deleting the parameter (deletion test: removes 4 dead arguments at the call sites in tests) would force tests to be honest.

[ADVISORY] The deleted test_state_results_multi_group_dupe covered the duplicate-group-key guard, and its replacement behavior (duplicate keys in group_vals silently overwrite with last-wins via `results[result.group_key] = result`, with the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error removed in processors/detector.py) has no test in this diff. A data packet containing duplicate group keys now silently drops all but the last result with no log signal; no test triggers duplicate keys in group_vals, so a future refactor back to a list or a change to the overwrite semantics regresses unnoticed, and operators lose the error signal the old code guaranteed.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, so its get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values/build_occurrence_and_event_data inherited bodies return None, and evaluating a detector of this type crashes instead of cleanly returning no results as before. Previously evaluate() returned [] for this handler; now get_group_key_values returns None so StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate fails with TypeError when iterating it (or, if abstract-method enforcement applies, instantiation raises 'Can't instantiate abstract class'), turning the old safe no-op into a crash in process_detectors for any detector registered with this grouptype.

[BUG] The change from list to dict (`results[result.group_key] = result`) silently overwrites a duplicate group key's result, and the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error that previously caught this condition was removed from process_detectors. When two group values produce the same result.group_key, one occurrence is silently dropped while process_detectors reports success and commits the merged state — the exact condition the removed log existed to surface now drops work with zero observability.

[ADVISORY] Occurrences are produced to Kafka via create_issue_occurrence_from_result during the evaluate loop, but the corresponding dedupe value and state updates are only advanced later via commit_state_updates, so the two sides of the dedupe guard are not committed atomically. If the process dies or an exception occurs after producing occurrences for an earlier group key but before commit_state_updates runs, the dedupe value is not advanced and reprocessing the packet emits duplicate occurrences with no error surfaced — an at-least-once side effect the caller cannot distinguish from success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the duplicate `group_key` guard in `process_detectors` (the loop that logged "Duplicate detector state group keys found" over a list result) and changes the handler API to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` instead of a list. The corresponding regression test for duplicates (`test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`) was deleted rather than replaced. However, this is more an API/observability behavior change than a directly verifiable functional defect within the new contract (the contract now implies uniqueness).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract from returning a `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to returning a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now builds that dict from `group_values`, which itself is a `dict` from `get_group_key_values`). With this new API, duplicate `group_key`s are not representable in the returned structure (dict keys are unique), and in the stateful path they are also not representable in `group_values` as shown in tests (`group_vals` is a dict). The removed duplicate-detection loop/log in `process_detectors` corresponded to the old list-based API; the deleted `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` relied on passing duplicate keys via a list (`group_keys=["dupe","dupe"]`), which no longer exists after refactoring. While it’s true the explicit log path was removed, the finding’s claim that “a data packet containing two entries with the same group key” will silently overwrite is not supported by the new dict-based interfaces shown in the diff.

Since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` does not implement the required abstract method(s), it remains abstract and attempting to instantiate it via `Detector.detector_handler` (used by `process_detectors` before calling `handler.evaluate(...)`) would raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`. The previous implementation provided an `evaluate` stub returning an empty list, so this change introduces a crash when this handler is exercised.

The OK/resolved path returns a `StatusChangeMessage` (see `evaluate_group_key_value` when `new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK`), and `process_detectors` will still call `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for it (`for result in detector_results.values(): if result.result is not None: create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)`), but there is no end-to-end test asserting the resulting producer call shape for this StatusChangeMessage branch. Existing assertions for resolution are only at the handler `evaluate()` level (e.g. `TestEvaluate.test_above_below_threshold`), not at the Kafka producer boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` non-OK branch, the code converts `new_status` via `PriorityLevel(new_status)` and passes it into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, which then sets `IssueOccurrence.initial_issue_priority=new_status.value` in the test helper. However, all added/updated tests drive the occurrence path only with `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` (e.g., condition creation in `create_detector_and_conditions` always uses `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH`). No test exercises occurrence creation for other non-OK statuses (e.g., MEDIUM/LOW), so the correctness of the enum conversion and priority propagation for those cases is not verified by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the diff adds `PriorityLevel(new_status)` where `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (see new call to `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))`). The diff provides no explicit mapping/validation layer to guarantee the two enums remain value-compatible. However, the finding asserts a concrete mislabeling bug if the enums ever diverge, which cannot be verified from the diff alone (we can't see the enum definitions or current value assignments). This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/maintainability concern introduced by the change, but not a demonstrable defect from the diff by itself.

With this API, duplicate group keys are not representable in the returned value (a dict can only have one entry per key), and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` iterates `group_values.items()` where `group_values` itself is a dict, so duplicates from the packet are structurally impossible. The removed duplicate-key guard in `process_detectors` was for list-based results; under the new dict-based interface there is no longer a meaningful place for that check in `process_detectors`.

In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` is an ABC that requires subclasses to implement abstract methods including `get_dedupe_value()`, `get_group_key_values()`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data()`. Since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of these, it remains abstract and attempting to instantiate it (e.g., via a registered `GroupType.detector_handler` used by `Detector.detector_handler`) will raise `TypeError` rather than behaving as the previous no-op stub.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Detector.project_id` is hardcoded to `return 1` (with an XXX comment) in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py`, and the newly-added occurrence-generation hook (`StatefulDetectorHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`) is now used when transitioning to a non-OK status. However, the core framework code in this diff does not itself set `IssueOccurrence.project_id` from `detector.project_id`; that mapping is only demonstrated in the test helper `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` where `project_id=handler.detector.project_id`. So the finding’s “every produced occurrence is stamped with project 1” claim is forward-looking/speculative for real handlers, but it is a concrete architectural/correctness concern exposed by this change because any real handler following this pattern would inherit the wrong project attribution until `Detector.project_id` is real.

However, in the shown stateful path `group_values` comes from a dict (`get_group_key_values`), so duplicates are not representable there, making this more of a lost-safety/diagnostic invariant than a directly verifiable functional defect in the current implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removed duplicate-group-key guard is silently replaced by dict last-wins overwrite, eliminating the error signal the previous implementation deliberately emitted. When a data packet produces two results for the same group key, the old code logged 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' at error level and skipped the duplicate; the new code (`results[result.group_key] = result`) silently overwrites the earlier result with no log, so the condition the old comment said 'we should investigate' becomes invisible in production and one status change is dropped without any trace. The dedicated test (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted rather than adapted, so the behavior change was never explicitly accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff the detector evaluation contract changes from returning a list to returning a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` (`DetectorHandler.evaluate` / `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). With a dict return type, duplicate group keys cannot be represented at the `process_detectors` boundary (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values` itself returns a dict, so input group keys are already unique). The removed test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` relied on passing duplicate group keys via a list (`group_keys=["dupe","dupe"]`), but the new API uses `group_vals` as a dict, which cannot carry duplicates. So the finding’s claim that production can now emit two results for the same group key and silently overwrite in `process_detectors` is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_state_results_multi_group builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with value=6 while the packet supplies 10, and the assertion still passes because build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its `value` argument entirely. The in-hook contract promises the occurrence is produced from the evaluated value; the test fixture hardcodes the same value (6) for every group and never asserts on it, so a regression where build_occurrence_and_event_data receives or embeds the wrong value (e.g. swapped keys, stale value from another group) ships green. Staff-level concern: the new coverage added in this diff cannot detect value-handling regressions in the exact behavior it was written to cover.
matched_golden_ids: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core discrepancy as the golden comment: the test builds/uses an expected occurrence for group_2 with value 6 even though the packet specifies group_2 should be 10, implying the test should use 10. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Adding build_occurrence_and_event_data as an @abc.abstractmethod on StatefulDetectorHandler is a breaking public-surface change to every existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclass outside this diff. Any out-of-tree or not-yet-migrated StatefulDetectorHandler subclass that only implemented get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values now fails at instantiation with TypeError (abstract method not implemented), turning what reads as a 'add a hook' change into a forced migration; the diff updates only the test mock and does not enumerate or verify the full set of concrete subclasses.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `@abc.abstractmethod` `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` to `StatefulDetectorHandler` (in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`) and calls it when `new_status != OK`. This is an API/surface-area change that forces all concrete `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclasses to implement the method to be instantiable. The diff updates the in-test mock subclass to implement it, but the diff itself does not demonstrate whether other subclasses exist elsewhere; thus the “breaks every existing subclass outside this diff” claim can’t be fully verified from the diff alone, but the breaking nature of adding a new abstract method is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every occurrence/event_data assertion in this diff is a tautology: the expected values are built by build_mock_occurrence_and_event, the exact same function the MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data implementation (line 35-38) delegates to, so the tests compare the code under test against itself and can never detect wrong occurrence content. If build_occurrence_and_event_data or the routing in evaluate_group_key_value passes wrong arguments (wrong group_key, wrong status, wrong fingerprint), the tests still pass as long as both sides call the same helper with the same arguments; proof: in test_state_results_multi_group the expected occurrence_2 is built with value=6 while the packet's group_2 value is 10, and the test passes because the helper ignores `value` entirely — a regression that propagated the wrong observed value into occurrences would be invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` delegates directly to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)`, and the tests also construct their expected `occurrence`/`event_data` using that same helper (e.g., `test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`, multiple `TestEvaluate*` assertions). This makes those assertions largely self-referential and weak at detecting incorrect occurrence contents or incorrect argument routing. The finding’s concrete example is verifiable: in `test_state_results_multi_group`, the packet provides `group_vals` with `group_2: 10`, but the expected `occurrence_2` is built with `value=6`; since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value` entirely, the test would still pass and would not catch a regression related to propagating the measured value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `value` parameter of build_mock_occurrence_and_event is dead — it is never referenced in the function body — yet every call site passes a value, creating the false impression that occurrence content depends on the observed value. The next implementer wiring real occurrence construction will copy this signature and tests will continue passing with any value, so a real handler bug that emits the wrong metric value in occurrences/evidence_data gets no coverage; deleting the parameter (deletion test: removes 4 dead arguments at the call sites in tests) would force tests to be honest.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., value: int, ...)` never references `value` in its body (it builds a fixed `IssueOccurrence` with `evidence_data={}` and no field derived from `value`). Yet multiple new/updated test call sites pass a `value` argument (e.g. `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, None, 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` and for multi-group). This can mislead future implementers/tests into thinking occurrence content is validated against the observed metric value when it isn't, reducing test coverage for wiring the real value into occurrence/event data. It’s not a runtime bug in the product code, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded test/fixture design issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The deleted test_state_results_multi_group_dupe covered the duplicate-group-key guard, and its replacement behavior (duplicate keys in group_vals silently overwrite with last-wins via `results[result.group_key] = result`, with the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error removed in processors/detector.py) has no test in this diff. A data packet containing duplicate group keys now silently drops all but the last result with no log signal; no test triggers duplicate keys in group_vals, so a future refactor back to a list or a change to the overwrite semantics regresses unnoticed, and operators lose the error signal the old code guaranteed.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff the duplicate-group-key scenario is effectively eliminated by the API change: `DetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds a dict keyed by `result.group_key`), so duplicate keys cannot coexist in the returned structure. Likewise, the stateful path’s inputs are now `group_vals` as a dict (`get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`), so duplicates aren’t representable at that stage either. The removed `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found")` and deleted test were tied to the previous list-based return type; the finding’s claim that “a data packet containing duplicate group keys now silently drops all but the last result” is not supported by the new types/flow shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, so its get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values/build_occurrence_and_event_data inherited bodies return None, and evaluating a detector of this type crashes instead of cleanly returning no results as before. Previously evaluate() returned [] for this handler; now get_group_key_values returns None so StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate fails with TypeError when iterating it (or, if abstract-method enforcement applies, instantiation raises 'Can't instantiate abstract class'), turning the old safe no-op into a crash in process_detectors for any detector registered with this grouptype.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[...]` with only `pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` defines abstract methods `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (all have `@abc.abstractmethod` and `pass`). Therefore `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is now abstract and cannot be instantiated; when `Detector.detector_handler` attempts to instantiate the group type’s `detector_handler`, this would raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`, turning the previous safe no-op `evaluate()` (which returned `[]`) into a runtime failure for detectors using this grouptype.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The change from list to dict (`results[result.group_key] = result`) silently overwrites a duplicate group key's result, and the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error that previously caught this condition was removed from process_detectors. When two group values produce the same result.group_key, one occurrence is silently dropped while process_detectors reports success and commits the merged state — the exact condition the removed log existed to surface now drops work with zero observability.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `DetectorHandler.evaluate` is changed to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds that dict from `group_values.items()`, where `group_values` itself is a dict). That makes duplicate group keys unrepresentable at the `process_detectors` boundary and (for the provided `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`) `result.group_key` is constructed from the input `group_key`, so two different inputs cannot yield the same `result.group_key` without an override not shown in the diff. The removed duplicate-key log in `process_detectors` corresponded to the old list-based API; with the new dict-based API, the specific “two results with the same group_key” condition described isn’t verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Occurrences are produced to Kafka via create_issue_occurrence_from_result during the evaluate loop, but the corresponding dedupe value and state updates are only advanced later via commit_state_updates, so the two sides of the dedupe guard are not committed atomically. If the process dies or an exception occurs after producing occurrences for an earlier group key but before commit_state_updates runs, the dedupe value is not advanced and reprocessing the packet emits duplicate occurrences with no error surfaced — an at-least-once side effect the caller cannot distinguish from success.

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, occurrences are emitted as a side effect inside the evaluation loop (`for result in detector_results.values(): ... create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)`), while state/dedupe advancement is only represented by queued updates in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` via `enqueue_state_update(...)` (and similar update tracking), with actual persistence deferred to `commit_state_updates()`. The diff does not show any call to `commit_state_updates()` in `process_detectors`, so producing to Kafka is clearly decoupled from persisting the dedupe/state guard, making the ordering/non-atomicity concern diff-grounded. However, the diff alone cannot prove where/when `commit_state_updates()` is invoked in the real pipeline (or whether at-least-once emission is acceptable), so this is best classified as an architecture/robustness concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect from the shown changes.
